meta.title: Our story — ZKward
meta.description: How ZKward started, what it does, and why we tell you when it loses money.

header.title: How we got here
header.subtitle: Five minutes. No jargon. Grab a coffee.

story.intro: The project used to be called ZkVanguard. People kept asking if we were a bond fund. It sounded like your dad's retirement plan. So we renamed it to ZKward. Same idea, slightly awkward to say out loud. You'll get used to it.

whatItIs.heading: What it is, in one sentence
whatItIs.body: A savings pool that trades for you and shows its math, so you don't have to take our word for it.

howItWorks.heading: How it works, plainly
howItWorks.body1: You put in USDC. A small crew of computer programs reads what people are betting on in prediction markets (like Polymarket) and lines up trades on crypto based on that. When it makes a trade, it also produces a little cryptographic receipt that anyone can check. The receipt proves the trade followed the rules. Without revealing your position.
howItWorks.body2: Think of it as an autopilot with a black box flight recorder. Except the recorder is public, and the autopilot won't take off in bad weather.

whereStarted.heading: Where it started
whereStarted.body1: A hackathon weekend. Too much coffee. One question: if computers move real money, why does anyone trust their reasoning? We thought we'd answer in two days. It took eighteen months.
whereStarted.body2: Along the way we won five hackathons and shipped on a handful of blockchains. Most of the test deployments lasted about an afternoon. SUI stuck. It's fast, cheap, and doesn't break when you look at it wrong. That's where the money lives now.

shipToday.heading: What we ship today
shipToday.item1: A real pool on SUI mainnet. Small on purpose. The contract itself caps deposits at $10,000. We wanted to prove it works before scaling. Slow is the point.
shipToday.item2: Eight safety switches that can pause the whole thing if something looks off. One tripped yesterday, after a rough day of testing (more on that below).
shipToday.item3: A learning loop: the AI grades its own trades, retrains overnight, and tries again. Sometimes it gets better. Sometimes it finds new ways to fail. We publish both.
shipToday.item4: An on-chain record of every deposit, withdrawal and transfer. Not a screenshot.

whyWeTell.heading: Why we tell you when it loses
whyWeTell.body1: Most projects only talk about their wins. Right now, our test traders are losing slightly on paper, and the signals have not yet shown an edge after costs. We're telling you because that's the whole point. If you can't see the losses, the wins don't mean much.
whyWeTell.body2: Also, hiding a loss is how a small loss turns into a much larger one three months later. We tried that once. Do not recommend.

whoBuilds.heading: Who's making it
whoBuilds.body1: Mostly one person, working from nine time zones away from most of you. Computer science degree, some years at big companies, an unreasonable number of side quests. Funded by savings and small grants that pay out roughly around the time the founder starts skipping lunch.
whoBuilds.body2: The paper trader has occasionally cost more per month than the founder eats. We consider this on-brand.

next.heading: Where this goes next
next.body: Two things need to happen. First, prove the trader stops losing money in the test pool. Then raise the deposit cap, one careful step at a time, with a real drawdown test at each step. If we skip a step, please yell at us on <telegram>Telegram</telegram>.

meta.title: FAQ — ZKward
meta.description: What ZKward is, how it works, what happens with your money, and why the paper trader is currently in the red.

header.title: Common questions
header.subtitle: Short answers. If yours is missing, email <email>ashish.regmi@zkward.com</email> and we'll add it.

q1.a: ZKward is an autonomous crypto vault. You deposit USDC. Six AI agents read prediction markets, funding rates, and price momentum, then trade across BTC, ETH, and SUI. Balances, shares and fees are recorded on-chain.

q2.a: No. A hedge fund is a regulated legal structure. ZKward is an on-chain vault: non-custodial, permissionless, no accreditation, on-chain fee accounting. Similar directional plays, with public on-chain records instead of quarterly letters.

q3.a: $10,000 total, capped by the Move contract during the operational-proof phase. Enforced on-chain — nobody, including us, can raise it without a governance action. The cap lifts step by step after each stage survives a real drawdown test.

q4.a: In a SUI Move object controlled by the pool contract. Non-custodial — your keys stay with you. Withdrawals are permissionless and available anytime.

q5.q: What is a STARK proof, and does ZKward use one today?
q5.a: A STARK proof lets anyone check a computation without seeing its private inputs. ZKward has an experimental prover, but today no trade carries a proof and nothing is verified on-chain. Our own review in October 2026 found the prover does not yet prove that a trade followed the vault rules. Until it is fixed and independently reviewed, rely on the on-chain records.

q6.q: What chains does ZKward run on?
q6.a: SUI mainnet is the lead chain (live pool at package 0x107292…7b726). Reference deployments exist on Hedera Testnet and Solana devnet. Portability is proven; production expands where demand justifies it.

q7.a: 50 basis points annual management and 10% performance on realised profits. Fees are routed through a MSafe multisig-held FeeManagerCap, distinct from the operational AdminCap. The fee path cannot be seized by an admin key compromise.

q8.q: Why is the paper trader losing money right now?
q8.a: Public transparency. We run paper traders against real signals and publish every trade — wins and losses. So far the signals have not shown a measurable edge after trading costs, so the books sit slightly below break-even. The running record is on the paper page. If we hid the losses, the wins wouldn't mean anything.

q9.q: How do I know the AI is not just making it up?
q9.a: You can check what it did, not why. Every deposit, withdrawal and transfer out of the pool is an on-chain transaction, and every signal source is scored in public against the price that followed. Trades also pass fixed limits: a 5-second cooldown, a 30-bps slippage ceiling and a leverage cap. There is no cryptographic proof of each decision today.

q10.q: Is ZKward safe against quantum computers?
q10.a: It does not depend on a proof system today. Funds are held by the SUI contract and moved by standard SUI signatures, like any other SUI application. The experimental STARK prover uses hash functions only, but nothing relies on it yet.

q11.q: Can I withdraw at any time?
q11.a: Yes. Withdrawal is permissionless. You sign a transaction, the contract calculates your share of the pool NAV, funds return to your wallet. There is no lockup, no notice period, no manager approval.

q12.q: How do I contact the team?
q12.a: Email ashish.regmi@zkward.com or join our Telegram (link in the footer). GitHub issues also work for technical questions.

zkDemo.title: Prove it without showing it
zkDemo.lead: This page makes a real zero-knowledge proof: it shows that a hedge stays within its limits without revealing the hedge. Change the numbers, make a proof, then check it.
zkDemo.hidden: The side, the leverage and the size stay private. Only the two limits are public.
zkDemo.proving: Making the proof, a few seconds…
zkDemo.refused: This hedge is outside its limits, so no proof can be made. That is the point.
zkDemo.rateLimited: Too many proofs from this connection. Try again in a minute.
zkDemo.error: The proof could not be made. Please try again.
zkDemo.checkLower: Check it against a leverage limit of {cap}
zkDemo.lowerRefused: Refused, as it should be: the proof was not made for that limit.
zkDemo.lowerAccepted: Accepted. That should not happen; please tell us.
zkDemo.statusHeading: What this is, and is not
zkDemo.statusDesign: A transparent ZK-STARK built on a hash function only, with no trusted setup and no elliptic curves, sized with a quantum attacker in mind.
